text: Administrator interviews follow a pretty predictable shape. This lesson walks through the stages, the core topics, and how to actually use your capstone as an answer bank.

Most processes run through some mix of four stages: a recruiter phone screen on your resume and qualifications, a hiring manager interview on behavioral fit, a technical round with scenario questions -- sometimes a live screen-share -- and occasionally a panel that repeats the same ground from different angles.

Be ready to explain, not just recognize: profiles, roles, and permission sets; org-wide defaults, role hierarchy, and sharing rules; when a validation rule is enough versus when you need Flow; and Data Loader versus the Import Wizard, including the data-quality tradeoffs of each.

The classic scenario question is "a user can't see a record they should see -- walk me through it." Interviewers grade the order: object and field access first, then org-wide defaults, then role hierarchy and sharing rules, then manual or Apex sharing last. Say each step out loud as you go.

Generic answers are forgettable. Pull real examples from your capstone: a real migration decision, a real security model choice and why you made it, something you genuinely learned by building it, and a moment where you pushed back on a shortcut that would have broken a best practice.
Next lesson: Developer interviews -- a different interview, built around a different skill set.
